artworks.title: The Great Windmill and the Rainbow
artworks.creditLine: Corcoran Collection (William A. Clark Collection, 1926)

artworks.title: Fair in Brittany
artworks.creditLine: Corcoran Collection (William A. Clark Collection, 1926)
artworks.description: This painting shows a busy marketplace scene at eye level with a crowd of people and cattle. Hills are in the distance under a cloudy gray sky, and in front of them we can see a line of rooftops and a tall church spire. In front of these buildings are the people and cattle. The people are indistinct, but many of them seem to wear white or red head coverings and clothes in earthy tones. The brushstrokes in the painting are thick and visible, giving the scene a blurred appearance.

artworks.title: Maternity
artworks.creditLine: Corcoran Collection (Museum Purchase, Gallery Fund, 1919)

artworks.title: The Pets
artworks.medium: oil on academy board transferred to hardboard
artworks.creditLine: Corcoran Collection (Gift of William Wilson Corcoran, 1869)
artworks.description: This painting shows a young girl sitting in a wooden chair, facing the right. She has pale skin, rosy cheeks, a slightly upturned nose, and long, brown hair put up behind her head. She is wearing a pale green dress and black shoes. To the right are several animals. On top of a table or counter is a small cage with two hamsters or gerbils with reddish-brown fur, surrounded by yellow straw and green grass. On top of their cage is a clear fishbowl on a tall glass stand, with a large goldfish and a smaller gray fish swimming in it. A small gray kitten sits on the cage, watching the fish, ears perked up and one paw slightly raised. Behind this counter and slightly to the left is a tall wooden stand with a bright green bird perched on it, surrounded by some potted plants. The bird has a blue head and small patches of red feathers on the tops of its wings. The girl is sitting on the edge of the wooden chair, watching the animals, a small silver plate and pitcher on the wooden floor by her feet. The wall and door behind her are light gray, and in some places, plaster appears have fallen off the wall, exposing a red surface underneath. Framed pictures hang on the wall, and on the right side we can see the edge of a window that casts pale light on the rest of the scene.

artworks.title: Hannah Lemmon Corcoran (Mrs. Thomas Corcoran)
artworks.creditLine: Corcoran Collection (Gift of Arthur Hellen, 1947)
artworks.description: The image is a portrait showing the upper body of a woman seated next to a wooden table. She is positioned facing slightly to the right, with her arm resting on the table and holding a small pink rose in her left hand. Her facial features include a calm expression, rosy cheeks, and visible brown eyes under dark, curly hair that frames her face, partly obscured by a white lace cap with decorative fabric elements. She is wearing a white, high-waisted gown with long sleeves with lace trim and delicate embroidery details. On the table, there is a small white vase with similar pink roses, adding a decorative element. The background consists of a deep green drapery.

artworks.title: Still Life with Silver Cake Basket
artworks.creditLine: Corcoran Collection (Museum Purchase through a gift of Josephine Boardman Crane, 1957)
artworks.description: In this painting, there is a tall, dark glass bottle labeled "Old Cherry" behind a decorative silver basket filled with various confections, including a slice of yellow cake with white frosting and several yellow biscuits or cookies, all arranged on a table. Positioned beside the bottle are two clear glasses filled with an amber liquid, with a silver knife and several pieces of yellow pastries scattered on the white tablecloth below the silver tray. In the background, a glimpse of greenery through a window is visible on the far right, with a white wall visible behind bottle in the center of the image, and the left side in shadow.

artworks.title: Roma Caves, Granada
artworks.creditLine: Corcoran Collection (William A. Clark Collection, 1926)
artworks.description: This painting depicts a white stone structure with a brown and gray roof surrounded by greenery and foliage. The walls and roof of the building are textured with the outlines of small stones, and the wall of the building directly across from us has a dark doorway at its center. Two people are visible on either side of this doorway. On the left, a person with light brown skin and short black hair stands with their hands on their hips. They wear a blue shirt and cream-colored pants, with a large tan necklace or garland around their neck. On the right, another person sits against the wall, wearing a bright yellow garment with pink and blue sleeves. They also appear to have light brown skin and black hair put up into two small bunches. Greenery hangs above the roof of the building, and the ground is depicted in dusty earth tones. The brushstrokes in the painting are thick and visible, and details, especially those in the people, are suggested with daubs of paint.

artworks.title: Marine
artworks.creditLine: Corcoran Collection (Edward C. and Mary Walker Collection, 1937)

artworks.title: Washington before Yorktown
artworks.creditLine: Corcoran Collection (Gift of the Mount Vernon Ladies Association, Mount Vernon, Virginia, 1944)
artworks.description: A man wearing a military uniform and riding a horse gestures in front of a small band of soldiers in this vertical painting. All the men have pale skin and wear navy-blue and flax-yellow uniforms. The central man, George Washington, and the cream-white horse he rides take up most of the composition. The horse has a glossy black mane and tail, and black hooves. The horse stands with its body facing our right in profile, one front leg lifted, but it turns its head to look off to our left with clear brown eyes. There is a scarlet-red blanket under the fawn-brown saddle. Washington also turns his head to our left to look up and off in that direction. He has a high forehead, a beaked nose, and his thin pink lips are pressed in a line. He has ruddy cheeks, a dimpled chin, and jowls along his jawline. His white hair is streaked with gray, and it sweeps back from his high forehead and bushes out over each ear. His blue jacket has gold epaulets, a high yellow collar around a white neckerchief, and gold-colored buttons down the front. The uniform also has yellow lapels, cuffs, and knee-high britches. The toe of his knee-high black boots pushes against the horse’s stirrup. Washington holds his right arm, to our left, out and points down with a gloved hand, which also holds a black, tricorn hat. The nearest man, just behind Washington to our left, rides a chestnut-brown horse. He is cleanshaven with blond hair, and looks at Washington, one hand tucked behind his lower back, where his hat rests on the horse’s rump. Several more men ride together under a grove of trees to our left, and the final rider lurches forward on a horse whose two front legs are raised midstride, to our right of Washington. The dirt ground beneath has some scrubby grass and a few plants. Tall, leafy green trees stretch to the sky to either side of the painting. The artist signed the painting in the lower left corner, on a rock. It reads, “Remt. Peale.”

artworks.title: Hillside at Étretat
artworks.creditLine: Corcoran Collection (Museum Purchase, Gallery Fund and William A. Clark Fund, 1959)
artworks.description: This painting depicts a rural landscape with a shepherdess tending to a flock of sheep on a tree-lined dirt path. She is facing away from us and wears a blue skirt with a white shirt and a white bonnet covering her hair. A green, grassy hillside with trees and grazing cattle is seen to the right, and the background on the left shows green fields and white cliffs under a cloudy sky.

artworks.title: William Cullen Bryant
artworks.creditLine: Corcoran Collection (Bequest of James C. McGuire, 1888)
artworks.description: The image shows a portrait of an older man. He has a high forehead with a bald top, framed by thick, wavy gray hair that extends into a full, bushy beard. His facial expression is neutral with a hint of a smile, and he has deep-set eyes. He is wearing a dark garment that appears plush and formal, possibly a robe or cloak, with a light shirt underneath. The background is dark and without detail, ensuring the focus remains on the man's face. He is not wearing any jewelry and is not holding any objects.

artworks.title: George Washington
artworks.creditLine: Corcoran Collection (William A. Clark Collection, 1926)
artworks.description: This painting is a portrait of a man from his chest up. He is positioned slightly angled to the left and looks directly at us. His skin is pale, and he has rosy cheeks, deep-set, dark eyes, a long, straight nose, and thin lips set in a neutral expression. His hair is light gray, combed back from his face and curled above his ears. He is wearing a black coat over a white, high-collared shirt and a white lace cravat. The background is dark brown.

artworks.title: Le Bas Meudon (A Curve of the Seine near Paris)
artworks.creditLine: Corcoran Collection (Edward C. and Mary Walker Collection, 1937)

artworks.title: The Willows
artworks.creditLine: Corcoran Collection (Edward C. and Mary Walker Collection, 1937)
artworks.description: Between us and a river lined with buildings on the far bank in the distance, tall willow trees nearly span the height of this horizontal landscape. The scene is loosely painted, and the color palette is almost completely dominated by cool tones of spring, sage, celery, and kelly green, and steel and sea blue. The grasses near us are painted with diagonal strokes that alternate direction and color as they move back toward the river. Golden yellow daubs in the lower right suggest blooms, and leaves on the trees are created with thin, upward strokes and dabs along slender branches. The trees reach high into a sky filled with sweeps of beige, blush pink, and spring green layered over pale blue. The river is a lavender gray, and the low, tightly clustered buildings are painted with a mix of ochre, peach, and denim blue. The artist has signed and dated the work in the lower right corner, though the final digit is illegible: “Claude Monet 188.”

artworks.title: A Difficult Line from Horace
artworks.creditLine: Corcoran Collection (William A. Clark Collection, 1926)

artworks.title: The Naturalists
artworks.creditLine: Corcoran Collection (Bequest of August M. Whittingham, 1980)

artworks.title: Landscape with Figures
artworks.creditLine: Corcoran Collection (William A. Clark Collection, 1926)
artworks.description: This horizontal painting presents a rural landscape scene centered on a dirt path that leads through a quiet countryside. The various brush strokes used, from smooth to textured, of oil paints on top of wood grain, combine elements of realism and landscapes. Starting at the lower left and moving across to the right, a wide, pale dirt road curves gently into the distance. The ground is uneven, with patches of grass and pebbles. Near the center of the composition, a woman with light skin stands on the path, her body facing away from us and slightly to the right. She wears a long dress with dull earth tones of reds, browns, and greens, and has light-gray colored hair. Besides her right, she holds the hand of a small child with light skin, who is dressed in darker clothing. Together, they stand atop a natural dirt bridge, walking along the curved path. To their left and rising above them, tall, dense trees and green-brown foliage dominate the scene. The trees' leaves contain shades of green and golden yellows, catching the soft, diffused light. On the right, a darker cluster of trees partially obscures a simple structure with a slanted roof, set back from the road. In the foreground at the lower right, a shallow pool of water reflects the sky in pale blue and gray tones. The sky fills the upper half of the painting with layered clouds, allowing warm light to break through, with a sun on the horizon. The overall piece utilizes colors of soft greens, browns, and grays, creating a calm, slightly hazy atmosphere

artworks.title: Harvest Moon
artworks.creditLine: Corcoran Collection (Bequest of Mabel Stevens Smithers, 1952)
artworks.description: The painting displays a dark green field stretching into the distance. A line of trees and small, indistinct structures can be seen near the center of the painting. One of the structures on the left shows a plume of smoke coming from a small chimney. In front of this structure is an indistinct person who appears to be wearing a dress. The color palette features earthy tones, with deep greens in the field and trees transitioning to softer browns and blues in the distance. The sky is light blue, but is partially obscured by grey and beige clouds. At the center is a yellow full moon, only slightly above the horizon and glowing warmly.

artworks.title: Weary Wayfarers
artworks.creditLine: Corcoran Collection (William A. Clark Collection, 1926)

artworks.title: The Letter
artworks.creditLine: Corcoran Collection (Edward C. and Mary Walker Collection, 1937)
artworks.description: One of two pale-skinned women standing by a window reads a letter and smiles in this vertical painting. Both women wear white caps. The woman reading the letter is the younger of the pair, and she stands to our left. She holds the paper to catch the light coming from the window, which is mostly covered with a white and pink-checked curtain. Her body faces us, but she turns her smooth-cheeked face to the letter in her hands. Her eyebrows are lifted, and her closed lips curve in a faint smile. She wears a wide-sleeved, black shirt over a white garment and a long brown skirt. The other, older woman to our right stand with her body angled to our left. She holds another piece of paper in one hand and clasps that wrist with her other hand. Her head tips away from us and she gazes down, facing our left in profile. Lines on her cheeks suggest her age. She wears a brown and black apron over a butter yellow, long-sleeved shirt that buttons at the wrists. Her hands are clasped in front of a marine-blue skirt. A table between us and the second woman holds two bowls, one with a wooden utensil, and a skein of red yarn with a half-knitted sock or stocking. The drawer facing us is open. The window is set deep into the thick wall, and a picture of a bearded man with long hair glowing with a gold halo hangs on the inside surface of the window frame between the women. The wall is mottled peanut brown.

artworks.title: Countryside in Picardy
artworks.creditLine: Corcoran Collection (William A. Clark Collection, 1926)
artworks.description: This painting depicts a landscape with an open green field stretching out into the distance. At the bottom of the painting, there is a rocky area with sparse vegetation and yellow, sun-bleached grass. Farther in the distance there are small groups of green trees, and some thatched-roof structures are partially obscured on the right. At the center of the painting there is a small area of red, suggesting a person or two walking along a brown path. Far in the distance there are small dots of white and pink, suggesting flowers or perhaps buildings. The color scheme is earthy and muted, dominated by browns, greens, and grays. The top half of the image is dominated by the sky, with textured white clouds swirling against patches of light blue.

artworks.title: Square in Paris
artworks.creditLine: Corcoran Collection (William A. Clark Collection, 1926)
artworks.description: The image shows a city street with grand old buildings, tree-lined sidewalks, and people going about their day. The architecture is detailed and rises into the sky. The brushstrokes are expressive, capturing movement. The color palette is soft with muted tones and hints of red. People walk and converse close by, while a horse-drawn carriage is seen in the distance.

artworks.title: Castle Gondolfo, Lake Albano, Italy
artworks.creditLine: Corcoran Collection (Gift of William Wilson Corcoran, 1869)
artworks.description: From a high vantage point, we look across hills, trees, and a body of water and into the deep distance in this horizontal landscape painting. A shed-like structure with an overhanging roof protecting an image of a woman holding a baby is near the left edge of the composition. In front of the structure, a person wearing a white head covering, red vest, white sleeves, and long blue skirt kneels on the dirt path, and a basket of flowers is near her knees. Two other people, all tiny in scale, stand nearby. One of them wears a brown cape, cassock, and hood, and the other wears a high-crowned hat, a red coat, gray pants, and holds a walking stick. Across the composition, a man sits and a woman stands, facing each other, on the far side of a boulder in the lower right quadrant of the painting. The man wears a burnt-orange jacket, slate-blue pants, a high-crowned hat, and holds a long staff. The woman has brown hair and wears a yellow dress over white sleeves and white lining across the neckline. They both have pale, peachy skin. A sailboat is reflected in the placid body of water that lies far below us, and a complex of buildings tops the hill on the opposite bank. The peanut-brown land flattens and ripples gently back to pale blue mountains lining the horizon, which comes just over halfway up this composition. White clouds pile up over the right side of the horizon, and a few thin clouds drift higher up. The upper corners of the canvas are darkened, suggesting that at one point this was displayed with an arched top. The artist signed and dated the painting as if he had written the information on the face of rocks in the lower right corner: “C.P. CRANCH 1852.”

artworks.title: Her Appeal to the Dauphin (Joan of Arc series: II)
artworks.medium: oil and gold leaf on canvas
artworks.creditLine: Corcoran Collection (William A. Clark Collection, 1926)
artworks.description: Dozens of people, all with pale peach skin, cluster tightly beyond a person kneeling at the center of this horizontal painting. The composition is filled from edge to edge with colorful patterns in the clothing, a wall-covering in the background, an area rug, and the tile floor, creating a collage-like effect. The men wear floor-length robes or tunics and stockings, and most wear hats or turbans. The women wear long, high-waisted dresses and tall, cone-shaped hats with veils or fabric draped from the peaks. Their garments are patterned in tones of burgundy, rust, and crimson red, forest and spring green, marigold orange, lemon and golden yellow, rose pink, and azure blue. The person kneeling at the center has chin-length blond hair, and wears a black, long-sleeved tunic, pointed black shoes, and gray stockings. That person faces our left in profile and raises a straight right arm to shoulder height, palm down and fingers extended, toward a standing man wearing a royal-blue robe to our left. Pale yellow, mauve-pink, and white flowers are strewn on the tiled floor in front of the crowd.
